lines.text: Let's explore the Nexon Fearless Plus P S petrol automatic.
We'll look at the cabin, family details and driving choices. You can steer the tour toward what matters to you.
The brochure lists a length of 3,995 millimetres and a wheelbase of 2,498 millimetres.
A personal visit is the place to check your driving position and the space around your passengers.
Three things to explore: front-seat ventilation, a seven-speed automatic, and standard safety equipment.
We'll put each alongside what you need from your next car.
This Fearless Plus P S petrol automatic has ventilated front seats; rear air vents begin at Pure Plus in the petrol and diesel range.
Six airbags, electronic stability control and ISOFIX are standard equipment.
Take in the side profile.
Tata lists 208 millimetres of ground clearance, with variation by trim. Keep that figure alongside the roads and parking spaces you use.
The brochure lists a width of 1,804 millimetres and a height of 1,620 millimetres. Check the dimensions against your parking space.
Smart and Pure use 195/60 R16 tyres; Creative and Fearless use 215/60 R16.
In this Fearless Plus P S petrol automatic, both front seats are ventilated, and rear passengers have their own air vents.
Try both rows when you visit.
Front-seat ventilation is listed for Fearless Plus P S in the petrol and diesel trim list. It isn't rear-seat ventilation.
Rear air vents begin at Pure Plus and continue through the higher petrol and diesel trims.
Here's the boot. Petrol and diesel versions are listed at 382 litres, measured to ISO V215.
For a stroller or weekend bags, bring your own and check the fit with the seats in use.
The CNG boot is listed at 321 litres using the same ISO V215 measurement basis. Capacity alone won't settle the fit of your luggage.
Creative Plus P S and Fearless Plus P S petrol and diesel trims have sixty-forty flip-and-fold rear seats, plus a rear armrest with a cup holder.
This Fearless Plus P S pairs the turbo petrol engine with a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic.
For stop-and-go driving, try its response on a test drive and see how it feels to you.
The 1.2-litre turbo petrol is listed at 88.2 kilowatts at 5,500 rpm, with 170 newton-metres at 1,750 to 4,000 rpm.
The diesel has manual and automated-manual options. CNG uses a six-speed manual; the seven-speed dual-clutch automatic is a petrol option, with availability depending on trim.
Six airbags, electronic stability control and ISOFIX are standard equipment.
Tata reports a five-star Bharat NCAP rating for petrol and diesel trims active in May 2026. Extra driver-assistance features depend on the trim.
For your child seat, ISOFIX is a useful starting point. Check the seat's compatibility and installation instructions before fitting it.
Fearless Plus P S petrol DCA also lists autonomous emergency braking and lane keep assist. Those features don't establish a safety ranking against another car.
Take a closer look at the cockpit: this Fearless Plus P S has a 26.03-centimetre touchscreen and a matching-size driver display.
On the petrol automatic, JBL audio with a subwoofer is another detail to try.
The touchscreen begins at Pure Plus; the matching-size driver display is listed on Fearless Plus P S in the petrol and diesel range.
Creative adds the surround-view camera and blind-view monitor; front parking sensors start at Creative Plus P S in the petrol and diesel range.
For the buying decision, get a current on-road quote for your exact variant.
Tata advertises a three-year, 100,000-kilometre warranty headline. Read the full written coverage and exclusions before deciding.
The advertised starting price is 7.39 lakh rupees ex-showroom, subject to change. It isn't a quote for this Fearless Plus P S automatic.
The Flexi offer advertises 6,499 rupees monthly for the first six months, with higher instalments after that. Final EMI and finance are at the financier's discretion.
We've looked at the cabin, family equipment and petrol automatic. The next useful check is how the seats, visibility and gearbox feel to you.
Choose Book Test Drive when you're ready, or stay here and ask another question.

The diesel has manual and automated-manual options. CNG uses a six-speed manual; the seven-speed dual-clutch automatic is a petrol option, with availability depending on trim.
Six airbags, electronic stability control and ISOFIX are standard equipment.
Tata reports a five-star Bharat NCAP rating for petrol and diesel trims active in May 2026. Extra driver-assistance features depend on the trim.
For your child seat, ISOFIX is a useful starting point. Check the seat's compatibility and installation instructions before fitting it.
On this Fearless Plus P S petrol automatic, the listed driver assists include autonomous emergency braking and lane keep assist.
Take a closer look at the cockpit: this Fearless Plus P S has a 26.03-centimetre touchscreen and a matching-size driver display.
On the petrol automatic, JBL audio with a subwoofer is another detail to try.
The 26.03-centimetre touchscreen begins at Pure Plus. The same-size driver display is listed on Fearless Plus P S in the petrol and diesel range.
Creative adds the surround-view camera and blind-view monitor; front parking sensors start at Creative Plus P S in the petrol and diesel range.
For the buying decision, get a current on-road quote for your exact variant.
Tata advertises a three-year, 100,000-kilometre warranty headline. Read the full written coverage and exclusions before deciding.
The advertised starting price is 7.39 lakh rupees ex-showroom, subject to change. It isn't a quote for this Fearless Plus P S automatic.
For selected variants, Flexi EMI is advertised from 6,499 rupees for the first six months, with higher instalments later. Final EMI and finance remain at the financier's discretion.
We've looked at the cabin, family equipment and petrol automatic. The next useful check is how the seats, visibility and gearbox feel to you.
